messages:
ingrid-corpit: Hey team — since yesterday afternoon our services can't complete calls to the Redwood Private control plane. App logs show TLS handshake failures, 502s intermittently. We use a corp proxy (Zscaler) + perimeter firewall. Any quick checks?

anna-support: Sorry you're hitting this — mTLS is required for the Private control plane. Can you paste a minimal curl/openssl debug output and confirm if you go through an HTTP CONNECT tunnel or if TLS is being intercepted by the proxy? Also which control plane FQDN are you hitting?

ingrid-corpit: FQDN is control.private.redwood.example (split-horizon). Quick paste from our CI job (sanitized):

```
$ curl --cert client.pem --key client.key --cacert ca.pem -v https://control.private.redwood.example/health
* About to connect() to control.private.redwood.example port 443 (#0)\n*   Trying 10.14.5.23...\n* Connected to control.private.redwood.example (10.14.5.23) port 443 (#0)\n* Initial HTTP request sent, awaiting response...\n* SSLv3, TLS handshake, Client hello (1):\n* SSL: no peer certificate available\n* curl: (35) SSL connect error
```

And our app logs have entries like: `tls: handshake failure` and on some requests `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` which is confusing because our certs are signed by the CA you provided when we onboarded.

sarah-corpit: adding corp-net team — we have a proxy that does TLS inspection by default. We can try a bypass rule but want to confirm root cause first.

michael-sre: Two likely failure modes: (A) outbound TLS is terminated by the corp proxy (TLS inspection) so client certificate never reaches Redwood, causing server-side mTLS failure; (B) the proxy rewrites SNI or replaces the server cert causing the client to fail server cert validation. We need packet captures from both sides (client-facing and egress-proxy-facing) to confirm.

raj-eng: Can you run an `openssl s_client` directly from a host in your VPC to the control plane IP and include the client cert/key so we can see the handshake trace? Example we prefer: 

```
openssl s_client -connect 10.14.5.23:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -CAfile ca.pem -servername control.private.redwood.example -msg -debug
```

Look for whether the server sends a `CertificateRequest` and whether the client sends a `Certificate` message in response. If the client cert never appears on the wire to the control plane IP, the proxy is likely intercepting.

ingrid-corpit: Ran the openssl command from a bastion behind the proxy (we also ran one from a host with proxy bypass):

From host BEHIND proxy (shows problem):
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
>>> TLS 1.3 Handshake [length 0005]
    ...ClientHello...
<<< TLS 1.3 Handshake [length 0030]
    ...ServerHello...
<<< TLS 1.3 Alert [length 0002]
    fatal: handshake_failure
write:errno=104
```

From host WITH proxy bypass (works):
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
... (handshake completes) ...
verify return:1
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=redwood-control
   i:/CN=redwood-ca
---
---
SSL handshake has read 4096 bytes and written 2345 bytes
```

sarah-corpit: So bypassing the proxy fixes it. That points to the proxy doing TLS interception and not forwarding the client cert. Our proxy vendor is Zscaler; we have an allowlist for CONNECT but not for passthrough for this FQDN.

anna-support: That matches expectations. Common fixes:
- Configure the proxy to allow TLS passthrough (no TLS inspection) for the control plane FQDN/IPs so the client->control-plane TLS is end-to-end and mTLS can happen.
- If proxy must intercept, configure the proxy to forward client certificate details (mutual auth via header) — but we DO NOT support header-proxied client certs for the control plane. We require raw mTLS.
- Ensure DNS split-horizon resolves to the private control plane IP from your network and that egress firewall allows direct TCP 443 to that IP.

michael-sre: To help eng look, please attach: `curl -v` output (with redacted certs if you like), the `openssl s_client -msg -debug` capture from the failing host, and a small tcpdump capturing the handshake with filter `host 10.14.5.23 and port 443` (PCAP). We want to confirm a proxy is presenting its own cert or returning the TLS alert. Also send the proxy product and version (Zscaler / Blue Coat / Palo Alto etc.) and whether it's doing TLS inspection or MITM.

ingrid-corpit: Uploading results now. tcpdump shows a client TLS ClientHello hitting the proxy, then the proxy issues its own TLS handshake back to the origin and we never see the client's Certificate on the connection to 10.14.5.23. Capture attached.

egress-proxy-bot: Automated check: destination IP 10.14.5.23 resolves from your network. Proxy detected: Zscaler TLS inspection enabled for domain pattern `*.private.redwood.example`.

raj-eng: Confirmed from the PCAP: server saw a TLS Alert 40 (handshake failure) with log `tls: client auth required but no client certificate presented`. That's exactly a downstream termination case.

ingrid-corpit: OK — corp-net can add an exception for `control.private.redwood.example` so it will use CONNECT passthrough (no TLS inspection). Do we need to whitelist any IP ranges on the Redwood side too?

anna-support: Thanks — after you configure passthrough please retest. You don't need to whitelist IPs on our side for the control plane if DNS still resolves internally; however we do require egress to the control plane IPs and to preserve SNI. If your proxy rewrites SNI you will still fail. If you prefer, we can provide the canonical control plane IP list for your environment to add to your firewall egress allowlist — let us know which region.

michael-sre: Also check that the client cert is not expired and your client is presenting the full cert chain if required. You can validate client cert with: 
```
openssl x509 -in client.pem -text -noout | grep -E 'Not After|Issuer|Subject'
```

ingrid-corpit: We added the passthrough exception in Zscaler and retried. From the same host: `curl --cert client.pem --key client.key --cacert ca.pem -v https://control.private.redwood.example/health` now returns 200 and the app is green. Thank you!

anna-support: Great news — glad that solved it. We'll mark this as a proxy TLS interception issue. For our internal notes: root cause = TLS inspection/proxy terminating TLS and not forwarding client certificate (mTLS broken). Remediation = enable TLS passthrough for control plane FQDN or add egress allowlist to bypass inspection.

raj-eng: Optional long-term: if your security team requires full inspection, we can discuss a short-lived VPN/peering or IP allowlist with preserved TLS to meet mTLS requirement, but that requires enterprise support.

ingrid-corpit: Filing ticket with corp-net to keep passthrough rule. Closing from our side once corp confirms policy. Thanks everyone. :tada:
